title: Fully quantum fidelity-based entropic continuity bounds
authors: Matthew Simon Tan, Ernest Y. -Z. Tan
abstract: We present a continuity bound for quantum conditional entropies in terms of fidelity, with no dependence on the dimension of the conditioning system. Our results encompass both the von Neumann entropy and one version of sandwiched Rényi entropy, which is particularly relevant for applications in quantum key distribution (QKD). In such applications, this bound should provide improved results as compared to previous continuity bounds based on trace distance. We also show that the bounds can be sharpened as expected for classical-quantum states, and verify that they hold when the conditioning system has countably infinite dimension. Finally, we present several variants tailored for exponential functions of the Rényi entropies instead, which should be relevant for QKD applications.
summary: This paper develops novel, fidelity-based continuity bounds for quantum conditional entropies, generalizing results from trace distance metrics. The bounds are shown to be applicable to both finite and countably infinite-dimensional systems. This work provides theoretically improved tools for quantifying state distinguishability, particularly relevant for quantum key distribution applications.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish continuity bounds for quantum conditional entropies using fidelity, providing an improvement over older bounds based on trace distance.
main_result: A continuity bound is derived for the difference in sandwiched Rényi conditional entropies, which holds even when the conditioning system has infinite dimension.
method: The authors use path integrals along the reduced great-circle path connecting two quantum states and apply differential inequalities derived from the fidelity metric.
model_or_system: The analysis concerns quantum states on a bipartite system (A and B), focusing on the conditional entropy $H(A|B)$ and its Rényi generalizations.
key_observables: Quantum conditional entropies (von Neumann and sandwiched Rényi), Fidelity, and the associated angular distance $\Lambda(ho, \sigma)$.
important_parameters: The Rényi order $\alpha \in (1/2, 1) \cup (1, \infty)$, and the dimension of the conditioning system $d_B$.
main_assumptions: The results are derived by analyzing paths of states and taking limits from finite-dimensional approximations to handle infinite dimensions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the bound for the general $\alpha$-variance, then deriving the bound for the von Neumann entropy limit, and finally presenting variants tailored for exponential functions of the Rényi entropies.
why_interesting: The development of tighter, fidelity-based bounds for entropy differences is crucial for quantifying distinguishability in quantum communication protocols like QKD.
